newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close mixed ahead of Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close mixed ahead of Wall Street.

text.p: Israeli shares closed slightly lower on Monday in mixed and selective trading as investors waited to see how Israeli high-tech stocks would fare in New York, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.53 percent, or 1.29 points, to 241.50 on all-share turnover of 136 million shekels against 194 million shekels on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.05 percent lower at 251.25.
"Trading was very mixed and selective today with small and medium capitalisation stocks leading the decline," said a trader at Bank Leumi.

"Investors are waiting for the opening of Wall Street to see what will happen with Israeli high-techs traded on Nasdaq. A strong decline of the American markets might trigger a short-term profit-taking," said Eran Goren, managing director of Zannex Securities.

"Today's decline is not a real correction and we are waiting for a more dramatic move. The fact that the market is declining on lower turnover is showing that this is a real bull market," Goren added.

The most active shares were Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which rose 1.0 percent to 1,830 agorot on volume of 9.4 million shekels, Israel Chemicals, which gained 2.75 percent to 341 agorot on turnover of 6.9 million shekels, and Koor Industries, which rose 0.5 percent to 33,307.
